items.title: Verdict system — how your calls count
items.detail: Two-tier = in-session one-liners count as decisions and a fresh-hands session ratifies feel; Strict = only rested day-start counts; All-count = any clear-headed call counts. Includes the shift-work amendment: 'rested' keys on hours into YOUR waking day (15:00-23:00 shift means home-at-midnight is your 17:00), never wall clock. Marathon sessions and dirty runs (god/slow-mo/runtime edits) stay PROVISIONAL under every option. On ruling: planning decision entry, verdict register seeded from the provisional backlog, game CLAUDE.md fresh-hands digest amended.

items.title: Adopt the repo rulebook (doc 18)
items.unblocks: the whole anti-drift system becoming law
items.detail: This is the rulebook born from your phone idea, designed properly with you in the remote session, and battle-tested by tonight's cleanup. Adopting it makes four habits law for every session in every repo: (1) THE LOGBOOK - one shared file in the planning repo where every pack handover, request between repos, and incident gets one line, so repos stop depending on someone remembering; (2) THE PASSPORT - no pack enters a repo without a small where-I-came-from slip (source, version, fingerprint), and importers refuse packs without one; (3) THE SESSION RECIPE - page 1 answers 'which repo do I open', including the janitor rules we used tonight (safety tags first, tests before pushes, you click anything destructive); (4) THE HANDOFF HOOK - every session-end handoff asks 'do I owe the logbook a line'. Adopting changes how sessions work going forward; it does not rebuild anything existing.
options: Not yet - I want changes first

items.title: Pack tools refuse to export unsaved/unpushed work
items.unblocks: never again losing a pack's recipe
items.detail: Every pack-making tool (tiles, worlds, world-filler, sprites, audio) gets one safety check: it refuses to export a pack while its own code has unsaved changes or commits that exist only on this machine. This is exactly what nearly made the game's character art unrebuildable - the art pack came from tool code no branch on GitHub contained. Tonight's cleanup found the same pattern again in a smaller way (a half-merged main that was never pushed). YES means each tool repo gets a small paste-ask to add the check in its own lane; the tools' behavior is otherwise untouched.
items.decision: Yes - all pack tools get the guard
options: Yes - all pack tools get the guard
items.lean: Yes - all pack tools get the guard

items.title: Talk-before-build becomes law
items.detail: Your own callout from the phone session, made into a standing rule: when a NEW tool, protocol, or system idea comes up, the design conversation happens in chat first - the agent builds nothing until you have walked through the idea and said build. (This exists because the first sync-protocol draft got built in one pass the moment you mentioned the idea, and you rightly called that out. The proper session afterwards agreed with the draft - but that was luck, not process.)

items.title: Finished packs also go up as GitHub releases
items.detail: Today a finished pack travels as a folder or zip handed from tool to game. This rule would ADDITIONALLY upload every shipped pack to its tool's GitHub page as a tagged release - so the original always lives online, any machine can download it, and its fingerprint can be checked forever. Costs a little ceremony per pack export. Honest lean: LATER - the current handover works, the logbook already fixes the forgetting problem, and the tester push matters more right now. Revisit after Gate 1.

items.title: Automatic drift check - now or later
items.unblocks: drift found by a script instead of a session
items.detail: A small report-only check that compares what each repo SAYS it holds (the logbook and pin file) against what is actually on disk and on GitHub, and lists mismatches. Honest lean: LATER - the rulebook's own principle is data first, tools after; let the logbook collect real entries for a while, then build the checker against real data. Building it now would be automating a file that is still nearly empty.
items.decision: Later - after the logbook has real data
options: Later - after the logbook has real data
items.lean: Later - after the logbook has real data
